items.title: China reaches 125 GW to become world's largest nuclear power

items.description: China has claimed the top spot globally for total installed nuclear power capacity, reaching 125 gigawatts, according to a blue book released Friday by the China Nuclear Energy Association. items.title: Trump reverses course, renews Russian oil sanctions waiver

featured_image.name: Trump ups sanctions on Russian oil

items.description:
The Trump administration on Friday issued a new month-long waiver allowing countries to purchase sanctioned Russian oil and petroleum products at sea, reversing its stated position just two days after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington had no plans to do so.[1][2]

The U.S. Treasury Department posted the license to its website late on April 17, permitting countries to buy Russian oil loaded on vessels as of that date through May 16. The license excludes transactions involving Iran, Cuba, and North Korea.[2]

items.title: Israeli fire kills two UNICEF water truck drivers in Gaza

featured_image.name: UNICEF says Israeli fire kills two Gaza water truck drivers ...

items.description: UNICEF said Friday it was "outraged" after two truck drivers it contracted to deliver clean water to families in the Gaza Strip were killed by Israeli fire at the Mansoura water filling point in northern Gaza. Two others were injured in the incident, which occurred during routine water trucking operations early Friday morning, according to the agency's statement.[1][2][3]

items.title: Israeli drone kills one in southern Lebanon hours into ceasefire

featured_image.name: Israeli drone attack kills 1 in southern Lebanon despite ceasefire deal

items.description:
An Israeli drone struck a motorcycle in southern Lebanon on Friday, killing one person on the first full day of a US-brokered 10-day ceasefire, even as President Trump declared on social media that Israel was "PROHIBITED" from bombing Lebanon.

Lebanon's state-run National News Agency reported that a motorcyclist was killed in the town of Kounine, in the Bint Jbeil district, after being targeted by an Israeli drone. The Lebanese army reported additional violations on Friday morning, including intermittent shelling of several southern villages and firing on an ambulance team in Kounine.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.description: Hours after declaring the Strait of Hormuz fully reopened to commercial shipping, Iran warned on Friday that it could shut the waterway again if the United States maintains its naval blockade of Iranian ports, escalating a standoff over one of the world's most vital energy corridors.

items.title: Iran's buried Pickaxe Mountain site looms over nuclear talks

featured_image.name: Inside Iran's top secret 'nuclear energy mountain'

items.description: As the United States and Iran inch toward a possible deal ahead of the April 22 ceasefire deadline, a deeply buried nuclear facility near Natanz known as Pickaxe Mountain has emerged as one of the most contentious obstacles to any lasting agreement — and some analysts and Iran hawks are pressing President Trump to consider extreme measures to destroy it.

items.title: Pakistan deployed fighter jets to escort Iran delegation home from talks

featured_image.name: Pakistani jets escorted Iranian delegation back home amid ...

items.description:
Pakistan's air force mounted a large-scale aerial operation to escort Iranian negotiators back from inconclusive peace talks in Islamabad, deploying around two dozen fighter jets and an airborne warning and control system after Iranian officials raised the possibility they could be targeted by Israel, Reuters reported exclusively on Friday.[1]

The escort mission, which took place on Sunday following the collapse of the first round of US-Iran proximity talks, underscored the extreme security risks surrounding the highest-level engagement between Washington and Tehran since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.

items.title: UNICEF reports 172 children killed as Lebanon ceasefire takes effect

featured_image.name: The impact of conflict on Lebanon's children - UNICEF Australia

items.description: A 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon took effect at midnight local time on April 17, offering a fragile pause in hostilities after 46 days of renewed war that has killed more than 2,100 people and displaced over one million. As the guns fell quiet, UNICEF reported that at least 172 children had been killed and 661 injured since fighting resumed on March 2, with more than 415,000 children forced from their homes.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran denies agreeing to hand enriched uranium to US

featured_image.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran

items.description:
Iran's Foreign Ministry on Friday flatly denied President Trump's assertion that Tehran had agreed to hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium to the United States, exposing a sharp public rift in fragile nuclear negotiations between the two countries.

"Iran's enriched uranium is not going to be transferred anywhere," Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told state television. He added that the "transfer of Iran's enriched uranium to the US has never been raised in negotiations".[1][2][3]

The denial came hours after Trump told CBS News in a phone interview that Iran had "agreed to everything," including a joint operation to retrieve the country's roughly 2,000 kilograms of enriched uranium and bring it to American soil. "Our people, together with the Iranians, are going to work together to go get it. And then we'll take it to the United States," Trump said, adding that no U.S. troops would be involved.[4][5]
